audit_findings.title: Acquisition earnouts are unbridged claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.112m recorded fair value ($0.91 per modeled share); $51.9m maximum potential payments ($2.60 per share)
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash without deducting the recorded contingent-consideration liability, overstating equity value dollar for dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: For agreements that contain contingent consideration caps, the remaining maximum amount of such potential future payments was $ 51.9 million as of June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: a $18.112m liability is filed and the bridge deducts none. Nevertheless, the recorded liability is only 0.7% of the $2,559m base equity value. Even the $51.9m contractual maximum is 2.0% of base value and would reduce the $148.13 bull value to about $145.53 per share, still far below the $204.15 market price. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the $18.112m current fair value from the equity bridge and verify that OE retains any $10.120m remeasurement benefit; separately disclose the $51.9m maximum exposure without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Convertible-note dilution does not match the modeled equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to 3.448273m excess denominator shares, equal to 17.3% of the 19.943287m modeled denominator; excluding them while holding other dilution constant computes to approximately $134.71 bear, $155.14 base and $179.08 bull per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Principal is a cash-settled debt claim already reflected through retained interest expense, while only conversion value above principal can create shares. Including full conversion capacities divides equity value by shares that the modeled intrinsic values would not cause to be issued.
audit_findings.evidence: The default settlement method is a combination settlement with a specified dollar amount of $ 1,000 per $1,000 principal amount of notes.
audit_findings.explanation: The settlement mismatch is demonstrated by the filed terms: principal must be paid in cash, and modeled values are below both the $191.98 and $353.82 initial conversion prices, implying no ordinary excess-value shares at those scenario values. The exact denominator composition is not supplied, but its 4.025221m excess over June 30 common shares is consistent with inclusion of the notes' 3.448273m combined capacities plus other dilution. A correction of the indicated size raises per-share values by roughly 21%, materially changing the valuation range and buy-below level even though the corrected bull value remains below the current price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile all 19.943287m denominator shares, remove full-capacity note shares, and solve each scenario using only cash-plus-excess shares under the 2029 and 2031 settlement formulas; rerun value per share and the 30% margin-of-safety threshold.

audit_findings.title: The full cash balance may not be distributable at par
audit_findings.magnitude: $82.761m of the $359.832m cash balance was held abroad; the entire cash bridge equals $18.04 per modeled share
audit_findings.mechanism: Taxes, restrictions, committed cash, or minimum operating liquidity would reduce the excess cash added to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Of this amount, approximately 23% was held by our foreign subsidiaries and subject to repatriation tax considerations.
audit_findings.explanation: The concern is unresolved rather than a demonstrated error: the filing identifies repatriation considerations but does not establish that the foreign cash is unavailable or quantify incremental leakage, and it records a $9.266m withholding-tax deferred liability on unrepatriated earnings. As a bounding comparison, removing the entire $359.832m cash balance—not merely the 23% held abroad—would lower the bull value from $148.13 to about $130.09 per share, still $74.06 below the $204.15 market price. Thus no possible haircut confined to the reported cash balance changes the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an excess-cash schedule covering minimum operating cash, restricted or committed balances, acquisition obligations, and incremental withholding taxes; replace $359.832m with the resulting net distributable amount.

audit_findings.title: Recurring restructuring and related costs may have been stripped as one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.591m FY2026 charges, equal to 10.6% of the $156.5m anchor OE; FY2024 and FY2025 charges were $6.391m and $5.335m
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back costs that recur in an acquisitive and repeatedly reorganized business raises anchor OE and every forecast cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: We may utilize similar measures in the future to realign our operations to further increase our operating efficiencies.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurring incidence is demonstrated by filed charges in all three years and management's statement that similar measures may be used again. The valuation error itself is not demonstrated because the OE worksheet is absent, so the record cannot show whether or how much of the $16.591m was added back. The possible amount exceeds 10% of anchor OE and is reasonably important, but the durable recurring allowance and after-tax effect cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE worksheet for every FY2024-FY2026 adjustment, classify termination, acquisition, integration, facility, legal and impairment costs, calculate an after-tax recurring allowance, and rerun all scenarios using the corrected anchor.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may not survive the runoff of major security contracts
audit_findings.magnitude: Contract revenue declined from $404m in FY2024 to $231m in FY2025 and $79m in FY2026; remaining FY2027-and-beyond OE contribution is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Failure to replace contract earnings would reduce normalized anchor OE and invalidate the bear-case assumption that FY2026 OE persists indefinitely.
audit_findings.evidence: Further revenues are expected to be recognized in fiscal year 2027 and beyond, albeit at relatively lower amounts as we have fulfilled the majority of equipment deliveries as of the end of fiscal year 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The runoff is filed, but an anchor overstatement is not demonstrated because most equipment deliveries had already run off before the FY2026 anchor, while consolidated Security revenue still increased and service revenue grew. The remaining decline is forward-looking, and neither contract margins nor replacement revenue are supplied. It should therefore be monitored rather than treated as a presently quantified valuation correction.
audit_findings.action: Track FY2027 contract revenue, gross profit and service carryover; obtain contract-level FY2026 OE contribution and rerun the valuation if post-runoff normalized OE falls below $156.5m.

audit_findings.title: Discrete tax benefits may remain in supposedly durable OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.8m FY2026 discrete tax benefit, equal to 3.7% of anchor OE; if fully retained, computed value sensitivity is approximately $3.46 bear, $4.09 base and $4.82 bull per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrepeatable tax benefit retained in net-income-based OE inflates the anchor and the operating-value forecast derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, we recognized a net discrete tax benefit of $5.8 million and $6.7 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $5.8m benefit is demonstrated, but its retention in OE is only a possibility because the OE worksheet is not supplied. Even assuming the entire benefit flowed into anchor OE and should be removed, the computed bull value would fall from $148.13 to about $143.31 per share, widening an already substantial discount to the $204.15 market price. The possible correction therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $5.8m benefit through the OE worksheet, separate equity-compensation and genuinely nonrecurring components, substitute a normalized cash-tax provision, and confirm that no SBC-related adjustment is duplicated.
